title: Soft-lock tokens and eviction-hinting for paged KV block allocator
author: Anna Morales
description: Motivation: paged KV cache eviction/pinning contention and fragmentation cause tail-latency regressions under mixed chat workloads. This change introduces a soft-lock token abstraction plus eviction-hinting metadata propagated from the allocator to the scheduler/kernel to improve reuse locality and reduce unnecessary full-page writebacks. Summary: add SoftLockToken lifecycle (acquire/release with soft timeout), eviction_hint bits on block descriptors, kernel-friendly batch eviction callback, and a heuristic reclaimer that prefers non-softlocked cold blocks for eviction. The allocator also collects per-block reuse-age histograms and exposes them to the console for rollout diagnostics. Design notes: soft locks do not prevent eviction permanently — they delay eviction for a short, configurable window (default 75ms) and allow cooperative prefetching; eviction_hint is a 2-bit field (PREFER_KEEP, SIGNAL_PREFETCH, NO_PREFERENCE) that informs scheduler to prefer keeping or prefetching an adjacent page during coalesced evictions; the reclaimer uses weighted frecency that gives a small bias to softlocked blocks to reduce churn. Safety and compatibility: changes are opt-in via runtime config `allocator.soft_lock_enabled` and `allocator.eviction_hint_mode` so clusters can A/B test behavior. Rollout plan: canary on 5% of host pools for 48h then progressive rollout. Benchmarks: unit microbench shows 8-12% reduction in 99th percentile decode latency under mixed small/long sequences, tail IOPS reduced ~15% and fragmentation (measured by free-block runs) improved ~18% on synthetic hot-prefix workloads. Testing: new deterministic allocator unit tests, stress test in perf-canary with 200k synthetic requests, and integration test in benchmark-lab against live models. Docs: short console UI addition exposes reuse-age histogram and soft-lock hit/miss counters. Implementation notes: careful lockless handoff to avoid ABA on descriptor updates, uses atomic CAS for descriptor state transitions, and a scoped RAII helper to ensure soft-lock release on error paths.
